title: Engineering Workflow
tagline: How I architect, engineer, test, and ship technical software from first principles.
philosophy: Great software begins with understanding constraints before typing code. I prefer explicit data models, minimal unnecessary abstractions, and building things from the ground up to understand how they work under the hood.
aiRole: I treat AI coding agents and LLM tooling as high-velocity pair programmers for scaffolding, exploring alternative implementations, and accelerating test coverage. However, every architectural boundary, memory layout, invariant check, and product decision is intentionally designed and verified by me.

stages.name: Problem Framing & First Principles
stages.summary: Strip the problem of preconceptions. What are the mechanical requirements? Is this best solved as a compiler, a native mobile app, or a lightweight CLI tool?
practices: Analyzing data flow and latency constraints before choosing frameworks
Evaluating whether external dependencies can be replaced with standard library code
Documenting core invariants and failure boundaries upfront

stages.name: Architecture & Schema Design
stages.summary: Design the data structures first. If the state representation and AST types are clean, the surrounding algorithms become significantly simpler.
practices: Defining strict TypeScript types or Rust enums/structs before writing procedural logic
Designing database schemas (Room/SQLite) and cache invalidation strategies early
Structuring modular Cargo workspaces or clean package boundaries

stages.name: Implementation & Pair Programming
stages.summary: Iterative development combining focused manual coding with AI agent acceleration. Code is written in small, verifiable increments with constant execution feedback.
practices: Writing core algorithms and engine loops manually to guarantee memory & time efficiency
Using AI assistants to generate test fixtures, edge-case tables, and standard API bindings
Maintaining readable, self-documenting code with clear symbol nomenclature

stages.name: Benchmarking & Edge-Case Testing
stages.summary: Testing beyond the happy path. In compilers: fuzzing syntax errors and recursion depth. In Android: verifying lifecycle pause states, orientation flips, and memory pressure.
practices: Profiling render loops to ensure 60–120Hz display refresh stability (OpenGL ES / Three.js)
Testing offline degradation when network APIs or cloud services are unreachable
Validating zero memory leaks across sustained background runs

stages.name: Deterministic Release & Distribution
stages.summary: Automated build verification through GitHub Actions CI/CD. Artifacts are validated for integrity, size constraints, and live URL health before deployment.
practices: Automated linting, TypeScript type-checking, and build validation gates in GitHub Actions
Automated SEO generation (sitemaps, robots.txt, and search indices) at build time
Publishing to production stores (Google Play Console) and static edge networks
